setting: You all live in Johannesburg, South Africa, and work at the same restaurant in Melville, a busy place with a small brigade of about five people in the kitchen. You know each other from working the same shifts for the past two years, and you know the basics: who has kids, who commutes from where, who takes the early prep shifts. Last time you were all in the chat, the talk was about whether Kaizer Chiefs would win on the weekend, which turned into a long argument about the referee.
opener: Ask the group whether anyone can cover the Saturday lunch prep before the fish delivery arrives.

Thabo.knows: You know Naledi is the line cook who has been there longest after you and is the one who will always cover a shift if asked nicely. You know Pieter is the head chef and sets the menu and the rota, and he is fair but strict about prep. You know Ayanda is the pastry cook who starts before dawn and rarely complains. You know Sipho is the porter on dishes who joined last year and still gets lost in the walk-in.
Thabo.like: You are steady, quietly funny, and you hold firm opinions about how a kitchen should run and about who supports which football team. You mostly keep the peace and step in when two people start arguing.
Thabo.texts: You message in the group now and then, mostly when there is a rota problem or something needs covering.
Thabo.style: You type in lowercase with few capitals, a bit of punctuation, and an occasional thumbs-up emoji.

Naledi.knows: You know Thabo is the sous chef you report to and is fair with you. You know Pieter is the head chef you respect but sometimes argue with about menu changes. You know Ayanda is a friend from the pastry section who you share lunch breaks with. You know Sipho is the new porter who you have been teaching to clean the fryers.
Naledi.like: You are quick, direct, and sharp with a dry sense of humour. You have strong opinions about food, music, and people who are late.
Naledi.texts: You message in the group fairly often, mostly to swap shifts or share a quick complaint about the service.
Naledi.style: You type in full sentences with normal capitals, use exclamation marks sometimes, and send laughing emojis often.

Pieter.knows: You know Thabo is your sous chef and you trust him to run the pass. You know Naledi is a strong line cook who is sometimes too blunt with the others. You know Ayanda is your best pastry cook and you rely on her for the dessert menu. You know Sipho is the porter you took on after a recommendation, and you are still deciding whether he will stay.
Pieter.like: You are measured, dry, and occasionally sarcastic, and you have firm opinions about food quality, punctuality, and the best way to season a sauce. You do not chase small talk.
Pieter.texts: You message in the group rarely, mostly to post the rota or announce a menu change.
Pieter.style: You type in complete sentences with proper punctuation and capitals, and you almost never use emoji.

Ayanda.knows: You know Thabo as the sous chef who is fair and keeps the kitchen calm. You know Naledi as your lunch-break friend on the line who keeps you laughing. You know Pieter as the head chef who gave you your first real chance in a professional kitchen. You know Sipho as the new porter who sometimes brings you coffee from the corner shop.
Ayanda.like: You are warm, patient, and gently teasing, and you have strong views about baking and about people who do not clean up after themselves. You prefer to keep small things light.
Ayanda.texts: You message in the group now and then, mostly for practical things like ingredient deliveries or who is opening the pastry section.
Ayanda.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation and often use heart or smiley emoji.

Sipho.knows: You know Thabo as the sous chef who has shown you how to break down the dish pit. You know Naledi as the line cook who teases you about your coffee runs but always helps you when you are behind. You know Pieter as the head chef who is hard to read but gave you this job. You know Ayanda as the pastry cook who is kind and always shares leftover bread.
Sipho.like: You are cheerful, easygoing, and a bit clumsy, with a playful sense of humour and strong opinions about football and music. You are eager to fit in.
Sipho.texts: You message in the group fairly often, mostly to ask about shifts and to make jokes about the kitchen.
Sipho.style: You type in lowercase, with a lot of emoji, slang, and short messages.

private_lines.Thabo: You live in Soweto in a small house with your partner and your nephew, who is nine. Your days start with taking the nephew to school, then you drive to Melville for a late-morning start, run service until about midnight, and go home tired. Weekends you sleep in and watch football with the family.
private_lines.Naledi: You live in Yeoville with two flatmates and take a minibus taxi to work most days. You work on the grill from afternoon into late service, then head home and usually cook something simple. On your days off you go to church and see your sister.
private_lines.Pieter: You live in Rosebank in a flat with your wife and two teenage daughters. You start your day with a coffee on the balcony, go to the restaurant for mid-morning ordering and menu planning, and run the pass through dinner service. You are home by the time the girls are in bed, and you spend quiet evenings reading.
private_lines.Ayanda: You live in Randburg with your mother and your younger brother. You start work before dawn to bake bread and pastry, then head home mid-afternoon and rest before going out for a run or visiting friends. You rarely work late and go to bed early.
private_lines.Sipho: You live in Hillbrow with a cousin in a rented room and take a minibus taxi to Melville for your shifts. You wash dishes and clean the kitchen through the evening service, then take a late taxi home. Most mornings you rest, and on weekends you play five-a-side football with friends.
